llm.summary: The skill largely does what it claims (monitor and analyze Google reviews) but its declared metadata omits the required Google Places API credential and the code reads credential files from an unexpected user-home path — these inconsistencies warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill is described as a Google-review monitor and the code implements Places API calls and web-scraping, which matches the purpose. However, the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or primary credential while the SKILL.md and code clearly require a Google Places API key (GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY or a credentials file). That mismatch between declared requirements and actual code is an incoherence the user should notice.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions stay within the review-monitoring domain (fetch via Places API, fallback scraping, parse HTML, store state, draft responses) and explicitly require human approval before posting. However, the code's get_api_key() reads credentials from Path.home()/.openclaw/workspace/credentials/google-places-api-key (an undocumented location) in addition to the local credentials/ file and env var. That access to a hidden home-directory path is not documented in SKILL.md/metadata and expands the skill's filesystem scope beyond what is described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only style) and the skill ships plain Python scripts (no external downloads or package installations). This is low-risk from an install mechanism perspective — nothing is pulled from arbitrary URLs or executed during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs a Google Places API key, but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. The code checks the GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY env var and also attempts to read credential files from two filesystem locations (one undocumented .openclaw path under the user's home). Requiring/reading an API key is proportionate to the purpose, but failing to declare it in metadata and probing an unexpected home-directory credential location is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true, does not request elevated system privileges, and stores only its own config/state under review-sentinel/state or the skill directory. It does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, verify and control where the Google Places API key will be read from and stored. Specifically: (1) Confirm the skill requires GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY (metadata should declare this); (2) Prefer providing the key via an env var rather than leaving a plaintext file in your home directory — the code will also look in Path.home()/.openclaw/workspace/credentials which is not documented in SKILL.md/metadata; (3) Review and, if necessary, modify fetch_reviews_places.py's get_api_key() to only read the credential location you trust (or to refuse reading home-directory paths); (4) Be aware the skill can perform web scraping (fetch_reviews.py) and will issue network requests to google.com and places.googleapis.com — ensure this is acceptable for your environment; (5) The skill stores state under review-sentinel/state in the workspace — check that stored review data is acceptable to keep locally; (6) Follow the SKILL.md guidance: do not enable auto-posting and require human approval for responses; (7) If you have sensitive business data (HIPAA or similar), review the code paths that include review text in outputs and ensure you comply with privacy requirements. If you are not comfortable with the undocumented credential file lookup, request the author to (a) declare GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY in the skill metadata and (b) remove or make configurable the home-directory credential path.
